headline: P0134 (Family Practice, GA): 99215 share of 12.8% vs 2.5% expected for its patient mix, elevated in every complexity band including low-complexity patients
rationale: P0134 billed 18 of 141 claims (12.8%) as 99215. Given this patient mix, about 2.5% would be expected (risk-adjusted score 2.85). The raw z versus peers is a modest 1.11, so the flag comes from the risk adjustment, not raw volume. The panel does not look unusually sick: 100 of 141 visits are for patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions, and only 3 are for patients with 4 or more. The provider's 99215 share is above the all-provider rate in every complexity band, including low-complexity patients (0 conditions: 4% vs 2.1%; 1 condition: 12% vs 3.4%). Sampled 99215 claims on low-complexity patients list simple diagnoses: a follow-up exam code Z09 (C0063715), an uncomplicated UTI N39.0 (C0063820), obesity alone (C0063709, C0063785) and osteoarthritis alone (C0063731, C0063768). The same osteoarthritis patient N0013 was billed 99215 on C0063731 and 99214 on C0063829. Billing is also skewed toward 99214, which makes up 89 of 141 claims (63%), and a 0-condition UTI visit was billed 99214 (C0063705). By contrast, the 4-condition heart-failure patient on C0063710 plausibly supports 99215. Together these points form a pattern consistent with upcoding. However, the claim lists are samples only, and no clinical notes, time records or MDM documentation are available, so nothing here confirms that any level was unsupported.
next_steps: Request the medical records for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims (C0063715, C0063820, C0063709, C0063785, C0063792, C0063780, C0063731, C0063768). Check whether medical decision-making or documented total time supports level 5.
Pull every 99215 claim and a sample of 99214 claims, not just this sample, to check whether high-level coding is concentrated on diagnoses like Z09, N39.0, E66.9 and M19.90.
Check whether time-based coding or prolonged-service documentation, such as counseling for obesity, is being used to justify the high levels.
Compare 99214 use (63% of claims) with Family Practice peers in GA, since level-4 overuse may be part of the same pattern.
Look at repeat 99215 billing for the same patient (P0134-N0050 on C0063785 and C0063792) and at inconsistent levels for similar visits (P0134-N0013).
